html:
The Pyu cities of Halin, Beikthano and Sri Ksetra, in the dry zone of central Burma, were walled cities of the Pyu people from about 200 BCE to 900 CE. They are the oldest cities in Burma.

The Pyu grew rice with irrigation, made coins and wrote in a script derived from Indian writing. They took up Buddhism early, and their large brick stupas came before those of Bagan.

Raids from Nanzhao in Yunnan in the 9th century broke their power, and the Burmans who settled at Bagan took over their lands and much of their culture. The three cities became Burma's first UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2014. See Theravada.
